blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: When persona-conditioned responses are read as respondent-level simulations, each response should reflect the described persona's knowledge, and the respondent written to know nothing must act as if the model's knowledge were not there. We test whether it can, and find persistent favourable-item real-twin rating separation under the tested low-knowledge and explicit-ignorance prompts. We define the resulting problem (knowledge leakage: a response bias that arises when knowledge the real user could not have enters the simulated response) and present a methodology for measuring it quantitatively. The core instrument pairs real items with fabricated twins matched in surface form: screened fabricated variants designed to minimize prior item-specific knowledge. The paired difference therefore provides a diagnostic contrast for knowledge leakage even in rating tasks where no answer is correct. In a rating experiment across three knowledge-handling arms and five API endpoints from two model families, we find, first, that the personas we test do not fully suppress real-item existence and familiarity signals: a favourable-item real-twin rating contrast remains under an explicit in-context statement that the persona has never heard of the item. Second, the unfavourable-item contrast reverses sign across domain groups: pooling all unfavourable-content items across domains the contrast sits near zero (+0.077 [-0.057, +0.204]), yet the same estimator in the same conditions returns -0.359 where the rating scale asks about an item's documented hazard and +0.438 where it asks about a company or an organisation. A pooled analysis of unfavourable-content items against zero therefore does not detect the opposing domain-group differences. All estimates are conditional on the adequacy of twin construction and screening; human low-knowledge baselines remain necessary for population-level interpretation.

Persona-conditioned rating is a simple form of user simulation: the model
receives a user description and produces the response that user would give.
The same failure mode could extend to interactive and agentic simulators,
including task-oriented dialogue and τ \tau -family benchmarks, whenever the
simulated user should not know hidden database state or the correct task
solution; leaked knowledge could make the user unnaturally cooperative and
inflate measured agent performance ( Yao et al., 2025 ; Seshadri et al., 2026 ) .

blocks.en:
The method rests on a premise that is rarely stated: each persona should
answer from its own described knowledge. But every persona is played by the
same model, which may hold documented facts about any item on the
questionnaire, and nothing guarantees that knowledge stays out of a persona
written not to have it. When facts the described user could not know move the simulated response, we call it knowledge leakage . Measuring it is harder than naming it. For subjective ratings there
is no correct answer that would expose a contaminated one, and asking the
persona whether it knows the item is circular: the answer is produced by the
same simulation being audited, and a persona that leaks knowledge into
ratings can also leak compliance into self-reports.

Our instrument breaks the circle with items designed to carry no stored
knowledge. For each real item we fabricate twin candidates matched in surface form
(same morphology and implied category), nonce terms with no evidence of
prior existence, screened so that no study model claimed recognition in the pre-run screening pass. Real items whose twin candidates were all discarded enter no analysis, leaving 178 valenced items. The persona
rates both; the twin is intended to absorb form cues, category priors, and
response style while carrying no detectable item-specific knowledge. Under
that matching assumption, a nonzero gap rejects the operational null that
explicit ignorance makes real and matched-twin ratings behave alike. What this requires of the twin is stated and tested in § 3 . The paired contrast works where no standard validation exists:
subjective ratings with no correct answer, no human reference, and only
black-box access.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Conditioning a model on demographic or biographical context to simulate
survey respondents was proposed as “silicon sampling” ( Argyle et al., 2023 ) ,
operationalised for replicating human-subject experiments ( Aher et al., 2023 ) ,
extended to economic agents and market research ( Horton et al., 2023 ; Brand et al., 2024 ) , and packaged into general social-simulation
frameworks ( Park et al., 2023 ) . Validation tempers the promise: simulated opinions are narrower than human
ones and skew toward model defaults ( Santurkar et al., 2023 ; Bisbee et al., 2024 ) ,
alignment varies across subpopulations ( Sun et al., 2024 ; Ma et al., 2026 ) , persona formulation changes the output ( Lutz et al., 2025 ) , human response
biases reproduce only selectively ( Tjuatja et al., 2024 ) , and persona surrogates
can collapse the heterogeneity of the population they stand in for ( Shi and Haupt, 2026 ) . Conceptual critiques warn against substituting model output for human
evidence without validation ( Lin, 2025 ) . Measured against real
users, the external-validity gap is material: agent success shifts by up to
9 percentage points with the simulator choice, with systematic
miscalibration across task difficulty and populations ( Seshadri et al., 2026 ) . That line measures whether simulated behaviour
matches human behaviour, not where a mismatched answer comes from; knowledge leakage is one unmeasured source.

blocks.en:
Parametric knowledge intrudes on instructed context: models answer from
memory against the prompt ( Zhou et al., 2023 ) and vary in receptivity to
counter-parametric evidence ( Xie et al., 2024 ; Wang et al., 2024 ) ; self-knowledge benchmarks target the model’s own knowledge rather than a
role-played character’s ( Laine et al., 2024 ) . Prior beliefs bias LLM-as-judge evaluations ( Zahraei et al., 2026 ) , models presuppose facts about entities rather than verify their existence ( Jung and Gonen, 2026 ) , and answerability studies show they often fail to flag
what cannot be answered ( Slobodkin et al., 2023 ; Yin et al., 2023 ) . Closest to our question, role-play studies document knowledge-boundary
violations directly: characters reveal knowledge beyond their point-in-time ( Ahn et al., 2024 ) , parametric knowledge pushes characters outside
their scope ( Sadeq et al., 2024 ) , Bhat et al. (2025) validate whether
persona agents correctly report and delimit their knowledge, and
persona-assigned models act on associations their explicit statements deny ( Gupta et al., 2024 ) . Together, these studies show that retained knowledge or dispositions can
conflict with task- or persona-specified boundaries.
Several of these works evaluate knowledge-boundary violations with verifiable
answers or self-reports; prior-belief-intrusion work also studies subjective
judgments. IPC focuses specifically on persona-conditioned real–twin rating
contrasts under operationalized ignorance.

blocks.en:
The fabricated-twin design borrows from two traditions. Psychometrics uses
overclaiming: seeding real knowledge items with plausible foils and reading
the foil endorsement rate as a measure of knowledge exaggeration ( Paulhus et al., 2003 ; Atir et al., 2015 ) . Related machine-learning work measures training-data extraction and
memorisation ( Carlini et al., 2021 ; Carlini et al., 2023 ) , evaluates unlearning on
fictitious ( Maini et al., 2024 ) and real content ( Eldan and Russinovich, 2023 ) , and
traces benchmark contamination via guided completion or rephrased samples ( Golchin and Surdeanu, 2024 ; Yang et al., 2023 ) . We combine the two: foils
built using surface-matching criteria, screened against the study models
themselves, used not to score a respondent but to give subjective ratings the baseline they otherwise lack.

For each real survey item we generate fabricated-twin candidates: screened
nonce terms matched in morphology and implied category, with no evidence of prior existence. The 178 valenced real items that retained a screened twin form the analysed battery; the rest were dropped before any rating was collected. The same persona rates
both under the same instructions (Figure 2 ). A rating of a twin can contain everything about the persona’s response style
and the item’s surface form, but no item-specific knowledge that survived
screening. The
impostor-paired contrast (IPC) is the real-item rating minus the paired twin
rating; d pos d_{\mathrm{pos}} and d neg d_{\mathrm{neg}} denote its mean over items whose
documented facts are favourable and unfavourable respectively; both are raw
rating-point differences on the 1–7 scale, not standardized effects. A nonzero contrast under a persona written to know nothing rejects the operational null that explicit ignorance makes real and matched-twin ratings behave alike, conditional on the twin being a fair stand-in and on the screening having worked. It is a diagnostic of incomplete suppression, not a unique separation of stored knowledge from residual form-based inference. Without a human comparison it does not say how far the ratings are from what real respondents would give.

Real items are obscure but verifiable terms in six survey domains
(supplements, skincare, food additives, household chemicals, brands, civic
organisations), valence-coded from fixed reference sources before any model
response was collected. The experiment draws up to 16 favourable and 16 unfavourable items per domain from a larger valence-coded source bank, which was itself screened with model outputs for obscurity; items whose twin candidates were all discarded in screening leave fewer in some domains, giving the 88 and 90 analysed. Twins were generated outside the evaluated families (a cross-family LLM plus
an algorithmic nonword resampler) and screened three ways before use:
character-gram, token-count, and surprisal checks intended to reduce surface-form
differences; an adversarial realness probe; and discarding variants that any
study model claimed to recognise. Matching was imperfect: stored whole-bank
token-count discrimination exceeded its target (Appendix A ).
Construction metadata also records finite exact-phrase attestation checks;
neither these checks nor non-recognition establish that a string never existed. The screening models are the study models, so the probe’s false-alarm rate is conditional on this selection. blocks.en:
Two conditions establish that the persona does not know the particular item: self-reported non-recognition (the gate answer) and explicit item-level ignorance (a context sentence naming the item). The rating experiment crosses five endpoints
(two providers), five persona-condition slots per domain (three low-knowledge
profiles, one expert profile, and a no-persona control), three knowledge-handling arms (a familiarity gate before the rating; the same gate after the rating; an in-context sentence stating the person has never heard of the specific item), and six domains; it additionally includes two instruction and two
question phrasings in a partially populated design, with scale direction
randomised within cells rather than fully crossed, for 145,560 trials over 404 distinct items. The explicit-ignorance arm runs only under the low-knowledge profile slots. The item is the unit of information, since trials of one item agree far more than trials of different items: each contrast averages the available per-(seed, endpoint) real–twin differences.
The primary explicit-ignorance slice has all 88 favourable seeds at each
endpoint and hence equal endpoint weight; gate-filtered slices may have
unequal coverage. Confidence intervals are bootstraps
clustered on the real-item seed, keeping each real–twin pair together
(10,000 resamples). Intervals quantify item-sampling uncertainty conditional on the tested
endpoints, personas, and wordings. The primary estimand is the same-arm d pos d_{\mathrm{pos}} under explicit ignorance; domain, matching, and
restriction analyses are exploratory. The result is not an averaging artefact: the trial-level superiority margin P ⁡ ( Y real > Y twin ) − P ⁡ ( Y real < Y twin ) P(Y_{\mathrm{real}}>Y_{\mathrm{twin}})-P(Y_{\mathrm{real}}<Y_{\mathrm{twin}}) , ties contributing to neither term, is + 0.176 +0.176 [ + 0.133 , + 0.220 ] [+0.133,+0.220] in the same-arm slice.

blocks.en:
A pooled check cannot see this failure. In our domain split, whether a rating
moves with an item’s documented facts varies with what the question asks, so averaging over question
types hides both directions at once, and a validation that compares pooled
marginals against a human reference can pass while the bias is present. The
audit we suggest is the instrument itself: seed the questionnaire with screened
twins and read the real–twin gap per question type rather than pooled. It
needs no human panel when used as a model-internal diagnostic and no access
beyond the API the survey already uses; population-level validation still
requires human comparison.

blocks.en: 6 Limitations
blocks.zh: 6. 限制

blocks.en:
The following limits bound what this shows. We never measure a genuinely low-knowledge
human, so these are divergences from the researcher’s specification rather than
from a real population; an expert persona free to use its knowledge separates favourable from
unfavourable items by at least 2.8 2.8 rating points, so the scale can resolve an
effect several times larger than the one we report, but without a human
baseline the direction of the resulting survey bias is not identified. Screening uses the study models themselves, so every estimate is
conditional on that selection: it removes twins the models admit recognising
but not those they deny, and held-out or cross-fitted screening would avoid the
resulting dependence; a single twin per item also leaves individual pairs
exposed to whatever that one string happens to carry. Real and fabricated strings differ lexically, so part of
the contrast may be inference from item form rather than knowledge of the item,
and we did not design a test that separates them. What the contrast does
establish is narrower and, we think, sufficient for the practical claim: within
these six domains and five endpoints, instructing a persona not to know
something does not make its ratings behave as though it did not.
The five tested endpoints are commercial APIs from two providers; the results
do not establish generality to open-weight models or other model families.
Multiple independent twins per item, held-out screening, low-knowledge human
calibration, and a within-item manipulation of question form would address
complementary validity questions; none is included in this study.
